generator: blender/galaxy2/galaxy2.py --all, baked under Blender 5.2's bundled Python (numpy only, every random draw seeded: two runs gave byte-identical plates). Rendered from a physical model (density-wave star formation, kinematic ageing, mixed-geometry per-channel dust, a 3D ray march for inclined views) and processed like an astrophotograph (PSF, asinh stretch).

conventions.colour: display-referred values for the dashboards' LINEAR pipeline: sample raw (three r128 default texture.encoding = LinearEncoding). Do NOT set sRGBEncoding: that decodes the plate (~gamma 2.2) and crushes the arms. Judged through the TV's final pass (exposure 1.45 -> ACES -> sat 1.12) and the wall's (x0.94, knee 0.62).
conventions.alpha: STRAIGHT (unassociated). rgb * a = the light the asset emits (premultiplied colour); a = max(R,G,B) of that light, rgb = its hue at full value (6-7 bit, smoothed ~1 px on the big plates; invisible at 1:1, it is what keeps a 2048^2 photographic PNG near 2 MB). rgb = 0 wherever a = 0. No premultiplied copy is shipped: texture.premultiplyAlpha would re-quantise the faint outskirts to 8 bits, while SrcAlpha * rgb in the blend unit keeps both 8-bit factors.

blend.additive: MeshBasicMaterial/SpriteMaterial {transparent:true, blending:AdditiveBlending, depthWrite:false} = (SrcAlpha, One): adds exactly rgb*a*opacity*color. Every asset here is light, so additive is the default. On a transparent canvas use CustomBlending One/One for colour and Zero/One for alpha so the page is not darkened.
blend.normal: (SrcAlpha, OneMinusSrcAlpha) also works for the galaxy plates: a tracks brightness, so a plate covers the sky behind its bright parts only (nearly identical to additive on a dark sky).

conventions.tint: draw with color 0xffffff: the plates carry their final colour. Remove mutedAccent()/desatMap() for these (they were for the old discs); the bloom should come from the core only.
conventions.orientation: row 0 = top. Galaxy plates: centred, face-on, transparent beyond `radius` (fraction of the half-width). Arms TRAIL for COUNTER-CLOCKWISE rotation as the image is viewed: spin counter-clockwise in image space (rotation.z increasing for a plane facing the camera).
conventions.sizes: galaxy plates 2048^2; the edge-on variant 2048x512; background galaxies 512-1024^2; clusters 512^2; nebulae 1024^2; PSFs 256^2; star disc 512^2; sky 4096x2048 equirect.
conventions.luma: luma = Rec.709 luminance of the premultiplied colour (rgb*a) measured from the shipped bytes; tv_display = ACES(1.45 * value), what the TV shows for that value at opacity 1.

discs.note: same shape as universe/manifest.json discs (paths relative to THIS manifest). Lookup order: the system id itself (sys:<id>, so an operator can pin a plate), then node:<index in /api/config nodes[]>, then pve_pool[system seed % 2] for any further Proxmox node so neighbours differ.

gold_edgeon.use: the SAME galaxy (model, seed, colours) seen 86 deg from face-on: cross-fade it in as a camera-facing quad (width = plate width) when the face-on plane is within ~20 deg of edge-on, where a flat disc would collapse to a line. Major axis horizontal; the near side is at the bottom.

v2.use: edge-on view of the SAME galaxy as gold_v2 (model, seed, colours), band-limited (no rain). Major axis horizontal; plate width = the face-on plate's width, so scale both quads alike.

sky.content: Milky Way band (warm bulge, dark rift that reddens), ~620k stars with a magnitude-limited colour mix, faint H-alpha / OIII / reflection nebulae near the plane, patchy galactic cirrus at high latitude, ~9000 tiny deep-field galaxies, and landmark objects (an M31-like spiral, two Magellanic-like clouds, a Pleiades-like and a Rosette-like cluster, a globular, an edge-on and an elliptical) so no 16:9 window is an empty void.

exposure.tv: sphere colour (tint) 0.35 for close-ups, 0.40-0.45 for wide shots (CONTRACTS 8a), raw sampling (the old plate used 0x333333 = 0.2 because it was brighter where it was busy). Measured on the 3080 Ti through the TV chain at 0.35: sky-only 6x4 cells 0.023-0.09 display luma (vignetted corners lowest). At 0.35 the darkest 5% shows ~0.008, the median ~0.031, the band ~0.362 on the TV: visible everywhere, well under any galaxy arm.
exposure.wall: as scene.background with raw sampling: multiply by ~0.30 (the wall grade does not lift it); skip restrainSky(), the plate is already restrained

v2.content: the v1 sky model at 8192x4096 with a second, fainter Milky-Way-like band crossing the first, more and fainter stars and field galaxies, landmark objects from the bg.v2 set; computed in float, dithered to 8 bits (no banding), JPG q88 4:4:4
v2.exposure: Start from v1's sky.exposure values and scale the tint by sky.luma.mean / sky.v2.luma.mean (both measured from the shipped bytes), then check the sky floor on your own display

soft.tint: multiply by the body's category colour
soft.size: sprite px = 24 x the core FWHM you want on screen (2 px core -> 48 px sprite); the halo then reaches ~10x the core, which is what makes a point read as a star
soft.note: every distant body: Moffat core + halo + r^-2.6 aureole; spikes have wavelength-scaled ripples (faint colour fringes) and are camera-fixed: billboard them, never rotate with the scene

hubble.size: sprite px = 24 x the core FWHM you want on screen (2 px core -> 48 px sprite); the halo then reaches ~10x the core, which is what makes a point read as a star
hubble.note: brightest few % only: two-vane (Hubble) diffraction; spikes have wavelength-scaled ripples (faint colour fringes) and are camera-fixed: billboard them, never rotate with the scene

jwst.tint: multiply by the body's category colour

corona_v2.colour: 5600 K warm white baked in; tint by multiplying
corona_v2.use: three sprites on ONE quad centred on the star: quad width = 2 r / limb (8 r). core = the photosphere (limb-darkened, granulated, premultiplied peak 0.92): skip it where the page draws the star as a lit sphere. halo = the corona: starts AT the limb (about 10 % inside it, never a flat disc), peak 0.45 just outside, ~(limb/r)^2.3 with soft streamers, zero before the sprite edge. flare = 6 thin diffraction spikes + 2 faint horizontal ones, nothing inside the limb, peak 0.60; camera-fixed (billboard, rotation 0). core + halo stays below the core's centre value at the limb.

rim_lut.format: single-channel L, 256 x 4, sample LINEAR, clamp
rim_lut.v_coord: row k is image row k from the TOP: v = (k + 0.5) / 4 unflipped, 1 - (k + 0.5) / 4 with three.js' default flipY

rows.0: lit-side atmosphere rim: rises from 0.80 R, peaks AT the limb (u 0.5), fades outward over ~6 % of the radius, zero by 1.16 R
rows.1: terminator ramp: day/night factor against N.L (soft twilight, 3 % night floor)
rows.2: night-side rim (forward scatter): thinner, peak 0.45 at the limb
rows.3: interior haze toward the limb (0 at 0.80 R, 1 at the limb, 0 outside)

ring_ice_v2.encoding: NOT a = max: rgb = ring colour, alpha = opacity; u = radius (inner -> outer), v = 64 rows of azimuthal variation; normal blending

ring_dust_v2.encoding: NOT a = max: rgb = ring colour, alpha = opacity; u = radius (inner -> outer), v = 64 rows of azimuthal variation; normal blending

stream_v2.tile: repeat along U, clamp along V
stream_v2.note: soft volumetric streak with dust motes; zero at both V edges; premultiplied peak 0.92

grain.format: single-channel L, mean 128, RMS 4/255, tileable both ways
grain.use: c += (grain - 128/255) * k * weight(luma); cycle the 3 frames
